name: Lermoos
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny village at the foot of the Zugspitze, featuring the family-friendly ski area Grubigstein and the Mohr-Lift.
beschreibung:
Overview

Lermoos is a historic alpine resort municipality in the Tyrolean Außerfern within the Reutte district and one of the premier destinations in the Tyrolean Zugspitz Arena. Perched at an altitude of 1,004 metres in a wide, sunlit valley basin at the foot of Mount Grubigstein, the village boasts iconic, unobstructed views of the imposing Wetterstein mountain range and the Zugspitze (2,962 m), Germany's highest peak. Home to roughly 1,500 residents, Lermoos pairs traditional alpine hospitality with world-class four-season sports infrastructure. The protected natural wetlands of the Lermooser Moos, advanced cable cars, and thrilling downhill mountain bike trails attract outdoor enthusiasts year-round.

History

Human activity in the Lermoos basin dates back to antiquity, when the Roman Via Claudia Augusta traversed the valley over the Fern Pass connecting Italy to the northern provinces. The community first appeared in historical documents in 1020 as Lari-Moos, referring to larch-covered peat wetlands. For centuries, Lermoos thrived along the lucrative salt transit routes linking Tyrol with Swabia, providing essential trade caravanserais and post stations. The grand baroque parish church of Saint Catherine was constructed between 1751 and 1753 by renowned architect Franz Kleinhans, showcasing exquisite rococo stuccowork. The opening of the Außerfern Railway in the early 20th century established Lermoos as an internationally recognized alpine ski resort.

Getting There

Lermoos boasts exceptional travel accessibility, including toll-free highway connections from Germany. Motorists arriving from the north travel via the German A7 motorway past Füssen and Reutte or take the B187 from Garmisch-Partenkirchen directly into the village. From Innsbruck and the south, drivers take the A12 Inntal Autobahn across the Fern Pass along the B179 federal highway. Rail passengers benefit from direct regional trains stopping at Lermoos station along the scenic Außerfern Railway connecting Munich, Garmisch-Partenkirchen, and Kempten. Frequent local ski buses link all villages across the Zugspitz Arena.

Tips

In winter, the Grubigstein ski domain offers 27 kilometres of diverse groomed slopes, modern gondolas, and scenic freeride runs set right against the village. The expansive Lermooser Moos nature basin provides a cross-country skiing and winter walking paradise featuring flat panoramic circuits framed by the sheer limestone towers of the Zugspitze. During summer, Mount Grubigstein becomes a prime mountain biking destination featuring celebrated singletracks such as the Blindsee Trail. Hikers should visit the rustic Tuftl Alm at 1,496 metres for traditional refreshments, while the Lermoos Panorama Pool offers refreshing summer swimming.
